settings.rationale: AI creation is disabled in every runtime mode.
Native construction validation may terraform eligible slopes automatically; the enabled source default is part of command behavior even though the reviewed route is flat.
Slope construction legality is read by native road, stop, and depot commands and therefore belongs to their frozen validation context.
The native dispatcher checks which construction commands may execute while paused; the replay must freeze that policy even at an unpaused boundary.
Native road-stop placement validation reads competitor-road permission and cannot inherit an undeclared user configuration value.
Native road-stop placement validation reads town-road permission and therefore requires an explicit frozen value.
The native competitor timer is disabled in addition to the zero AI-company limit.
Construction prices must remain on the selected low-cost table for the funding proof.
Disasters add unrelated vehicles, timers, and map mutation.
Only the explicitly created coal mine and power station may exist.
Native affordability and command rejection must remain observable.
The source-defined minimum interest is frozen because ledger state is authoritative.
The initial loan ceiling affects company financial state.
No AI company may be created after the fixture boundary.
Subsidy offer lifetime is frozen even though the selected route has no awarded subsidy at the replay boundary.
The payment multiplier is frozen so any unexpected subsidy state cannot silently alter the ledger.
Breakdown RNG and service routing are excluded from the first fixture.
Vehicle purchase and running costs feed the exact ledger.
The retained zero-population town may not rebuild road tiles into the frozen map.
Cargo aging directly affects the native delivery payment calculation.
The payment setting is frozen even though the two-stop plan contains no transfer order.
The native economy command policy remains explicit so an undeclared configuration cannot enable a different company-ledger action surface.
Coal production rate must use the unscaled source-defined value.
Inflation would alter every construction, vehicle, and payment amount over time.
Periodic infrastructure charges are outside the minimal payment loop.
The source-defined twelve-minute calendar year fixes the calendar timer threshold.
Calendar tick behavior is the selected authoritative time basis.
The fixture town cannot grow houses or roads into the route.
Frozen economy prevents industry production changes and closure.
The empty-world generation and native fixture creation seed are immutable inputs.
Coal mine, power station, cargo, and vehicle tables are climate-dependent.
OpenTTD stores the 64-tile X dimension as exponent 6.
OpenTTD stores the 64-tile Y dimension as exponent 6.
The native empty-world surface height is an explicit fixture-generation input.
The start year determines engine availability, prices, dates, and industry state.
Autosave is disabled to prevent filesystem side effects; it cannot enter projected game state.
Exit autosave is disabled to prevent undeclared save writes; it cannot enter projected game state.
Replay controls the boundary directly; this client-only toggle cannot enter projected state.
LinkGraph solver accuracy is future-relevant whenever a graph exists and remains part of the saved settings even though manual distribution keeps the first fixture graph empty.
LinkGraph demand weighting is frozen to prevent an external setting from changing packet routing if graph state becomes reachable.
LinkGraph supply weighting is frozen to prevent an external setting from changing packet routing if graph state becomes reachable.
Armoured-cargo distribution remains manual so no LinkGraph job or automatic packet destination can enter the experiment.
Manual cargo distribution avoids link-graph jobs and routing state.
Mail distribution remains manual so automatic LinkGraph routing cannot introduce hidden continuation state.
Passenger distribution remains manual so automatic LinkGraph routing cannot introduce hidden continuation state.

The runtime graph recalculation interval is 16 seconds: the empty isolated configuration starts from the table value 8 days and the pinned compatibility path multiplies it by CalendarTime::SECONDS_PER_DAY (2) before fixture creation.

The runtime graph calculation duration is 64 seconds: the empty isolated configuration starts from the table value 32 days and the pinned compatibility path multiplies it by CalendarTime::SECONDS_PER_DAY (2) before fixture creation.
The native short-path saturation threshold changes flow allocation when a graph exists and therefore belongs to the frozen continuation context.
Loading cadence changes the first-loading and departure boundaries.
Station loading selection affects the captured cargo path.
A no-breakdown vehicle must not take an automatic depot detour.
Station cargo selection affects which waiting cargo the road vehicle captures.
The road-vehicle queue model changes road-stop entry and blocking behavior on the declared route.
The YAPF search-node limit can turn a reachable route into a no-route result and must remain explicit.
The maximum depot detour penalty participates in native depot route choice and service behavior.
The crossing penalty is an exact YAPF route-cost input even when the reviewed route contains no crossing.
The curve penalty changes exact YAPF costs and tie resolution along the declared route.
The slope penalty is an exact YAPF route-cost input even though fixture validation declares the road plan flat.
The occupied-bay penalty affects native stop approach selection and queue behavior.
The occupied drive-through-stop penalty affects native route choice and vehicle queue interaction.
The base road-stop penalty changes exact YAPF costs for paths through stops.
Disabled modified catchment selects the source-defined radius four for truck stops.
Industry-station association behavior is frozen even though both industries are original non-neutral types.
Station construction/join behavior is frozen even though each stop is one tile.
Exactly one road vehicle is required and no extra pool breadth is needed.
Normal availability rules must prove the selected engine is available in 1950.
Driving side affects lane position and road-vehicle movement state.
The original acceleration model is the narrower first movement path.
The movement parameter remains frozen even though fixture validation forbids slopes.
Service interval interpretation is fixed to calendar days.
Zero disables scheduled servicing during the bounded replay.
